newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners shun expensive foreign crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners shun expensive foreign crude.

text.p: U.S. refiners still shunned foreign spot crude due to poor arbitrage economics and a wide choice of alternatives in a bearish climate, traders said.
The latest American Petroleum Institute (API) report late Tuesday showed a huge build of 9.3 million barrels in crude oil, which helped put off refiners' requirements.
"The build in Padd 3 and the WTI/Brent arbitrage is not helping U.S. refiners enter the market," a Midwest trader said, noting that demand for North Sea barrels was subdued.
Speculation a U.S. Gulf refiner picked up 1.0 million barrel of Oseberg for Nov 1-15 Monday could not be confirmed.
Traders said it was possible the seller moved barrels west at an attractive price to remove excess supplies from the depressed European market.
Delivered Brent was pegged notionally at Monday's offer level of West Texas Intermediate +15 cents cif for second-half November, with Oseberg seen within similar ranges.
In nearby markets, a cargo of Oriente for late November was valued at WTI -$2.60/70 cif, while Cano Limon was pegged at Dec WTI -$1.40 or Jan WTI -$1.00 fob.
U.S. after-markets were relatively thin with a full cargo of Dec Brent done at $22.25 a barrel, and a partial at the same price, up about eight cents from London's IPE close.
Inter-month Dec/Jan changed hands at +32 cents, within the same range at the earlier London session.
